semantics.desiredOutcome: An exact current released organizational claim can enter one bounded domain-local execution path without widening organizational work-selection or acceptance authority.
semantics.currentState: Integration B is delivered on main but current post-merge repair is addressing one remaining lifecycle-publication currentness race; writer-authority/idempotency and transition-revision repairs are already preserved.

requiredBehaviors.statement: Execution begins only from an exact current released organizational claim.
Execution attempt currentness is resolved before policy or strategy selection.
One immutable execution-attempt binding pins the exact work contract, release, policy, strategy, runtime and configuration used by that attempt.
Recovery of the same semantic attempt reuses the same immutable binding instead of silently selecting a new strategy or runtime.
Execution result, runtime fact, verification evidence, domain acceptance and authoritative publication remain separate states and authorities.

invariants.statement: Organization owns WHAT, WHO and execution authority; domain execution control owns HOW for the already-released claim.
Execution policy is not a work scheduler.
Execution strategy cannot select another organizational work item or dispatch another domain.
A successful runtime result is not equivalent to acceptance or authoritative publication.
In-flight execution remains bound to the exact selected strategy and runtime identity across recovery.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A stale or non-current released claim cannot acquire executable domain-local authority.
Crash and restart preserve the same semantic execution-attempt binding.
A later policy or strategy revision cannot mutate an already-bound in-flight attempt.
Verification demonstrates that domain execution cannot widen into cross-domain scheduling or organizational lifecycle control.
The delivered slice stops before cross-domain continuation, ProductStateProjection, deployment and Product QA.
